articles.title: Climate breakdown: Is the EU adapting to the new normal? Europe's summer of disasters
articles.description: It has been called Europe's disaster year. 2026 has seen more than 30,000 excess deaths linked to heatwaves, along with mega wildfires, nuclear power plants having to shut down, gas plants under pressure, droughts reducing hydropower generation from rivers and wild fluctuations in electricity prices, not to mention major disruptions to crops and farming in general.

articles.title: 'Iran has dragged us into this conflict,' top Emirati diplomat Anwar Gargash says
articles.description: In an interview with FRANCE 24 on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly, Anwar Gargash, senior diplomatic adviser to the UAE president, said Iran "has dragged us into this conflict", after the UAE was "the target of 3,300 missiles and drones" fired by Iran. After US President Donald Trump said he could either negotiate with or "obliterate" Iran, Gargash warned that the "current situation of no war, no peace is not sustainable".

articles.title: Macron says ‘military resources’ to be sent to Saudi Arabia
articles.description: Speaking to broadcasters TF1 and France 2, French President Emmanuel Macron on Thursday announced that “military resources” will be sent to protect the Yanbu oil site in Saudi Arabia, integral to maintaining the kingdom’s fuel exports and increasingly threatened by Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthi rebels.

articles.title: Trump made ‘final decision’ to allow Ukraine to produce Patriot missiles, Zelensky says
articles.description: President Donald Trump told President Volodymyr Zelensky that he had made a "final decision" to grant Kyiv the licence to produce Patriot air defence missiles, the Ukrainian leader said Friday. The assurance came during the last meeting between the two leaders, Zelensky said, capping a period of uncertainty after a series of reversals on the issue.

articles.title: Nepal’s catastrophic floods were ‘warning to the world', PM Shah tells UN
articles.description: Nepal’s Prime Minister Balendra Shah said on Thursday that last month’s catastrophic floods were a “warning to the world” of growing climate risks in the Himalayas. He said warming was melting glaciers and permafrost and urged international support to help Nepal adapt to threats it could not face alone.

articles.title: Top European leagues demand FIFA reforms, piling pressure on Infantino
articles.description: FIFA president Gianni Infantino came under increased pressure Friday as Europe's four main football leagues called for sweeping reforms of the world football governing body. The English Premier League, Spain's La Liga, Italy's Serie A and Germany's Bundesliga demanded that measures are adopted to ensure "disciplinary matters remain demonstrably insulated from political interference".

articles.title: REPLAY : Pope Leo XIV arrives in France for four-day visit
articles.description: Pope Leo XIV has landed at Paris Orly Airport for the start of his four-day visit to France. A welcoming ceremony was held on the tarmac in the presence of President Emmanuel Macron, marking the beginning of a programme combining diplomatic meetings with major public events across Paris, Lourdes and Metz.

articles.title: France's Catholic influencers take faith from social media to real life
articles.description: Catholic influencers gathered hundreds of young people for an evening of prayer at Paris's Saint-Sulpice church ahead of Pope Leo XIV's visit, highlighting how social media is becoming a new tool for evangelisation. As youth baptisms rise in France, creators say their goal is to turn online engagement into real-life communities, while Church leaders warn that influencers themselves should not overshadow the faith they promote.

articles.title: Pope Leo XIV's Paris agenda includes Macron meeting and Notre-Dame visit
articles.description: Paris is making final preparations for Pope Leo XIV's first official visit to the French capital in 18 years, with volunteers welcoming crowds ahead of his four-day trip. His programme includes meetings with President Emmanuel Macron and UNESCO, a popemobile procession, a prayer service at Notre-Dame, a youth vigil at the Stade de France, and a mass at Place de la Concorde expected to draw up to one million people before he continues to Lourdes and Metz.

FRANCE 24's Rochelle Fergus

articles.title: ‘Most powerful force is human potential’: Ukraine's military prioritises new tactics, technologies
articles.description: François Picard is pleased to welcome Kyrylo Berkal, Deputy Commander of Ukraine's Third Army Corps, He sees Ukraine’s struggle centred on human potential, adaptation and will. While Ukraine is outnumbered, outgunned and sometimes outflanked, their answer is to make human initiative a weapon: giving soldiers and sergeants room to innovate, developing technology from the tactical level upward, and trying to outthink their adversary. Berkal says that Operation Vivaldi embodies that philosophy.

articles.title: EU vows to pursue €120 million fine on X after US backs Musk's court challenge

The bloc fined the platform in 2025 for breaching EU online transparency rules, notably with its pay-to-play blue "verification" checkmark.

articles.title: Saudi reports fresh Houthi attacks as France pledges to defend key oil port

France said it would send military assets to help protect the Saudi oil terminal at Yanbu. The strikes came amid renewed fighting in Yemen that has killed dozens, according to sources cited by AFP.

articles.title: 'Moldova is the best performer in my class': EU Enlargement Commissioner Marta Kos
articles.description: The EU has gone through seven waves of enlargement since 1973, but there has not been one since Croatia joined in 2013. Indeed, there are not likely to be any new members in the club before 2028 – some 15 years after Croatia entered. But 2026 undeniably has momentum, and is on track to be a record year in terms of opening and closing new chapters for existing applicants. That is why our guest, EU Enlargement Commissioner Marta Kos, sees this as "the year of the enlargement."

articles.description: Le pape est attendu à Lourdes, samedi. Un moment fort de sa visite en France, pour lequel la ville se prépare déjà, tout comme la pilote du vol que va emprunter le souverain pontife pour rejoindre les Hautes-Pyrénées.

articles.title: Affaire Thélyson Orélien : le concepteur de Pangram, Max Spero, n’a « aucun doute » sur la présence d’IA dans le roman « C’était ça ou mourir »
articles.description: En trois ans, le logiciel de détection d’IA est devenu l’un des plus efficaces de son secteur, déclenchant de multiples controverses aux Etats-Unis. Pour son concepteur, « Pangram pourrait finir par ressembler à une étiquette nutritionnelle ou de certification 100 % bio » de la prose écrite.

articles.title: Comment s’inspirer du management de Zinédine Zidane pour mener votre propre équipe vers la victoire
articles.description: La méthode Zizou a été éprouvée avec succès au Real Madrid. Plusieurs axes vont être répliqués avec les Tricolores. Quelles pourraient être les déclinaisons en entreprise ?

articles.title: A Saint-Avold, la dernière centrale à charbon de France s’inquiète pour sa reconversion
articles.description: La centrale Emile-Huchet, en Moselle, se trouve de nouveau en danger. Relancée six mois après sa fermeture, en 2022, pour faire face à la crise énergétique, elle avait pourtant décroché, en 2025, une loi devant assurer sa reconversion au gaz et au biogaz.

articles.title: Mathieu Bock-Côté : «Affaire Thélyson Orélien, le roi est nu»
articles.description: CHRONIQUE - Après avoir multiplié les compliments les plus emportés à l’égard de C’était ça ou mourir, une part du milieu littéraire refuse d’admettre l’imposture, lui préférant, encore et toujours, le logiciel antiraciste.

articles.title: C’était ça ou mourir : l’Académie Goncourt supprime de sa liste le roman, le Renaudot et le Femina s’interrogent
articles.description: Le romancier québécois est soupçonné d’avoir écrit avec l’aide de l’intelligence artificielle, ce qu’il conteste avec son éditeur, Grasset.

articles.title: L’Ethiopie, géant africain rattrapé par la guerre : qui sont les belligérants, quels sont leurs objectifs ?
articles.description: La guerre a repris en Ethiopie, géant démographique de la Corne de l’Afrique. Les combats opposent différents groupes rebelles, constitués le plus souvent sur des bases ethniques, à l’armée fédérale. Dans cette mosaïque complexe, les renversements d’alliance sont fréquents.

articles.title: «C’était très français» : à l’Élysée, Emmanuel Macron et la République se pressent autour du pape Léon XIV
articles.description: RÉCIT - Le président a dit vendredi la «grande joie» que représente le voyage en France du pape, qui a fait passer des messages fermes tout en prenant le temps de saluer les représentants de l’État et de la société, loin d’être indifférents à sa présence.

articles.title: Euthanasie, laïcité, enseignement catholique : à l’Élysée, Léon XIV appelle les chrétiens à s’impliquer dans la société française
articles.description: En présence d’Emmanuel Macron et de nombreuses personnalités, le pape a insisté sur le droit à la vie, dans le contexte récent de l’adoption de la loi sur l’aide à mourir.
